verses.sa: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् । इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥
verses.tr: This much I have gained today; I will get this desire fulfilled. This wealth is mine now, and more will be mine again.
verses.angle: Idam: the word that claims everything
verses.speaker: Unknown

intro.text: Here, Krishna shows the inner speech of a mind trapped in endless acquisition. Listen for the voice that claims ownership over the past, present, and future.

body.text: This much I have gained today; I will get this desire fulfilled. This wealth is mine now, and more will be mine again. The speaker uses the word idam, this, three times, and the word me, of me, twice, claiming ownership over every object and every future gain. That same deluded mind then declares, I am the lord, I enjoy, and I am happy.

verses.sa: असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि । ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥
verses.tr: That enemy has been slain by me, and I will slay the others too. I am the lord, I enjoy, I am accomplished, powerful, and happy.
verses.angle: Aham: the word that repeats seven times
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen closely to one word that keeps returning in this verse. It is the root of every claim made by the arrogant mind.

body.text: That enemy has been slain by me, and I will slay the others too. I am the lord, I enjoy, I am accomplished, powerful, and happy. The word is aham, I. It repeats seven times in this single verse, each time a new claim of ownership: I am the lord, I enjoy, I am accomplished, I am the master of strength, I am happy. The text shows how this same delusion of I and mine leads to endless sacrifice and giving.

verses.sa: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥
verses.tr: We are rich, surrounded by many people. Who is equal to us? We will sacrifice, give, and enjoy. Deluded by ignorance, they think this way.
verses.angle: The deluded 'I' claims its own sacrifices
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the mind of an enemy who claims to have already won. Now he shows how that same pride speaks, and what it plans to do with its wealth.

body.text: We are rich, surrounded by many people. Who is equal to us? We will sacrifice, give, and enjoy. Deluded by ignorance, they think this way. The deluded mind is full of 'I'. It says, 'I am rich, I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice.' It turns even charity and worship into proof of its own greatness. Krishna then says that such people, trapped by desires and confusion, fall into misery.

verses.sa: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः । प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥
verses.tr: Deluded by many desires, trapped in the net of confusion, and deeply attached to pleasures, people fall into a lower realm of misery.
verses.angle: Mohajaala: the net that catches the attached
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues describing those who are not free. Listen for the trap that catches them.

body.text: Deluded by many desires, trapped in the net of confusion, and deeply attached to pleasures, people fall into a lower realm of misery. Mohajaala, the net of delusion, is the trap itself. A mind caught in this net is not merely confused by many desires, but is also attached to those very pleasures, ensuring the fall into misery. Krishna then shows what happens when pride and wealth make people pretend to perform sacrifice.

verses.sa: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः । यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
verses.tr: Self-important, stubborn, drunk on wealth and praise, they perform ritual in name only, with pretence and without proper method.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: If you see someone performing elaborate rituals, how do you know if the act is pure? Krishna names the warning signs hidden inside the act itself. Listen for the mask.

body.text: Self-important, stubborn, drunk on wealth and praise, they perform ritual in name only, with pretence and without proper method. Listen to dambhena, pretence. They perform rituals in name only, without proper method, and with arrogance. The outer action remains, while the inner sincerity is missing. Those who act from ego and anger hate Me, who dwell in their bodies and in the bodies of others, and they find fault with My qualities.

verses.sa: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः । मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥
verses.tr: Those who take refuge in ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger hate Me, who dwell in their own bodies and in the bodies of others, and they find fault with My qualities.
verses.angle: Ego, force, arrogance, desire and anger
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna names the inner habits that make a person hostile to the divine presence within themselves and in others. Listen to how he connects them.

body.text: Those who take refuge in ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger hate Me, who dwell in their own bodies and in the bodies of others, and they find fault with My qualities. Krishna lists five inner habits, ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger, and says those who take refuge in them hate Me, who dwell in their own bodies and in the bodies of others. He then warns that He casts these hateful people into demonic births again and again.

verses.sa: तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् । क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥
verses.tr: I cast those hateful, cruel, and vile people again and again into demonic births.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna draws a line between a life of cruelty and a life of peace. Listen for the word that tells us what happens to those who choose cruelty.

body.text: I cast those hateful, cruel, and vile people again and again into demonic births. Krishna names himself as the one who casts the hateful and cruel down. He does not let them drift; he sends them again and again into demonic births as the consequence of their own actions. Those deluded beings born into shadowed births sink into a lower state and never reach the divine.

verses.sa: असुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि । मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥
verses.tr: Those deluded beings, born again and again into shadowed births, never reach me and sink into a lower state.
verses.angle: mamah, reaching Krishna, is the only way out of the shadowed birth cycle
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the dark nature of destructive people. Now he shows the end of that path, where the deluded are trapped in shadowed births.

body.text: Those deluded beings, born again and again into shadowed births, never reach me and sink into a lower state. Notice how the verse pairs two ideas. The deluded enter shadowed births birth after birth, and they do so because they never reach me. The shadowed birth is not a random fate; it is the direct result of never turning toward the divine. Krishna then names the three gates of ruin that keep people locked in this cycle.

verses.sa: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
verses.tr: Desire, anger, and greed are the three gates of ruin. Abandon these three.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna names the three inner enemies that block the path of right action. Listen to how he groups them.

body.text: Desire, anger, and greed are the three gates of ruin. Abandon these three. Krishna does not list these as separate sins. He calls them a threefold gate, a single entrance that leads the self into ruin. Freed from these three gates, a person acts for their own good and reaches the highest state.

verses.sa: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः । आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
verses.tr: Freed from these three gates of darkness, a person acts for their own good and reaches the highest state.
verses.angle: Freed from darkness, one acts for highest good
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After naming the three gates of ruin, Krishna now asks what happens to the person who walks through them. Listen for the path that opens up.

body.text: Freed from these three gates of darkness, a person acts for their own good and reaches the highest state. Krishna says that once a person is freed from those three gates of darkness, they act for their own highest good, and from that action they reach the highest state. But Krishna warns that a person who ignores this path and follows only their own desire will not find happiness or the highest state.

verses.sa: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः । न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥
verses.tr: Whoever sets aside scripture and acts on desire alone does not attain perfection, happiness, or the highest state.
verses.angle: Desire alone blocks all three goals
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just listed three inner gates of ruin. He now warns what happens when a person ignores right guidance and acts only on impulse.

body.text: Whoever sets aside scripture and acts on desire alone does not attain perfection, happiness, or the highest state. The verse names three losses, one after the other, showing that a life driven only by desire misses the highest aim. Krishna then tells Arjuna to treat scripture as his only authority for deciding how to act in the world.

verses.sa: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ । ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, scripture is your authority for deciding what should be done and what should not be done. Knowing the duties laid out in scripture, you should act here in the world.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna concludes his teaching by offering a single standard for deciding right and wrong action. Listen for the word that names that standard.

body.text: Therefore, scripture is your authority for deciding what should be done and what should not be done. Knowing the duties laid out in scripture, you should act here in the world. The word is shastram, scripture, and it is called pramanam, authority, for deciding what should be done and what should not be done. Arjuna then asks about those who worship with faith but set aside scriptural rules.

next.title: As a person's faith is, so is the person
